doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Growing up and learning drums in Washington
title: Tommy Myles's band, Leo Parker and Rick Henderson
summary: Brower asks about the Lincoln Colonnade band of Tommy Myles; Cobb says it was before his time, but he knew Malachi and played with Leo Parker and Rick Henderson.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Did the name Tommy Myles – does that mean anything to you?

He had the band at the Lincoln Colonnade that I understand that in his band – I’ve actually seen pictures – John Malachi was in that band, Tommy Myles’s band. Tommy Potter was in that band. I’m trying to think of the arranger – Jimmy Mundy was also . . .
Jimmy Mundy. Yeah. I know those names.
That’s before me, then. That’s before I got to the scene.
You would have been – this is late ’30s.

Yeah, well, I wasn’t there yet. I didn’t get there until maybe about ’41, ’42, somewhere around in there. I just probably was not even – got interested in listening to the music. By the time that happened they was probably in and out of that situation you just mentioned. But I knew Malachi. A little later we got to be good friends. A little later I got to play with Leo Parker and guys like that, because they lived there.
Was this after Leo came back?

Yeah, it’s after Leo came back. Was a lot of good things happening around here. Between the time I started to play and the time I left, I did a lot of good things. Worked with Rick Henderson. Rick Henderson was about my age, but he was way far ahead in music than I was, because he was a good alto player and he could make arrangements.
. . . and places like that, after I got so I could play a little bit.
